abstract: Adenosine-to-inosine (A-to-I) RNA editing can recode transcripts without permanently altering the genome. ADAR-catalyzed editing depends on both local sequence and RNA secondary structure, making it difficult to anticipate which sites will be edited or how mutations will change their activity. Moving from observing endogenous A-to-I editing to using it as a programmable molecular tool requires predicting how editing responds to sequence changes. Here, we present ModFormer, a model that integrates RNA sequence representations with predicted secondary structure to predict ADAR-mediated editing. Trained on human data, ModFormer predicts editing sites and rates across substrates and species unseen during training, recovers established sequence and pairing preferences, and anticipates experimentally measured responses to RNA mutations. These predictions prioritize responsive sites in mutational screens and guide an autonomous AI agent toward candidate RNA designs. ModFormer provides a framework for predicting how sequence changes reshape RNA editing and can be adapted to new substrates with limited experimental data.
